bull.b: A 20-year, 401 MW Anthropic lease and monetization of the Abernathy JV materially increase contracted, predictable revenue and free up capital. This shifts revenue mix toward long-duration cash flows and funds owned-campus expansion, reducing reliance on volatile spot bitcoin mining over the multi-year buildout.

Rapid ramp in HPC leasing demonstrates early product-market fit for contracted compute. Combined with management guidance of high adjusted HPC margins and improving adjusted EBITDA, this structural shift can deliver steadier, higher-margin revenue versus mining once scale and tenant cadence persist.

Substantial cash and project-level balances provide the company the financial runway to complete multi-year campus buildouts and absorb execution timing risk. That funded pipeline reduces near-term dilution risk and supports disciplined capital deployment into contracted or near-commercial assets.

bear.b: Persistently negative operating and free cash flow means core operations do not self-fund growth and the company remains reliant on external capital or asset monetizations. Over a 2–6 month horizon, continued cash burn magnifies execution and financing risk if project timing or monetization outcomes slip.

Negative equity and prior extreme leverage reflect volatile capital structure and constrained financial flexibility. This raises the probability of covenant, refinancing, or rating stress and increases dependence on asset sales or dilutive raises to fund development if cash needs outpace planned liquidity sources.

bear.t: GAAP earnings volatility from noncash items
bear.b: Large noncash fair-value swings and impairment charges create headline earnings volatility that can obscure operational progress and complicate capital markets access. Persistent mark-to-market exposure on warrants or recurring impairments can impair investor confidence and increase cost of raising long-term capital.
